honestyNote: PARTIAL BUILD, filed as one. What is done and green: the writer's decision core (`src/lib/ledger-cutover-ab-cells.mjs`) and its 25 pre-registered falsifiers, in a PR against hauska-factory origin/main 0f4558a4. What is NOT done and is not claimed: the job wrapper (writer-allowlist + cli + cloudbuild chain), the engine retrieval-api cell reader, and the store-side counts. Two findings that moved the plan, both verified at source and each recorded in premisesCheckedBeforeUse: (1) the reader leg is BLOCKED in hauska-engine alone, because the serving slate is a byte-pinned vendored copy of LDT's literal whose divergence guard fails on any pair this repo invents -- so the reader cannot ship before LDT's literal moves, and LDT's own vendoring precedent says a pair may only be added once its parcel_gate_verdict reads pass; (2) the doc_repo RAIL_POLICY diff is NOT the only site -- hauska-factory's gate-exclusion-classifier.mjs holds a SECOND, hand-typed copy of the same mid-cutover classification and still names all three rails.

scope.whyTheseBoundaries: The dispatch's item 1 is 'write each rail's cell from the same source that serves it today', and every downstream leg (the gate grade, the reader, the policy move) is decided by WHICH CELL KIND each atom state produces. That mapping is the whole risk: A-214's rule (a join miss is not a verified absence) is a cell-kind decision made once per atom state, and the one county in the set with zero boundary atoms county-wide (McLennan) fails silently if it is got wrong. So the boundary is drawn around the mapping and its falsifiers, and everything that only SELECTS FROM a correct mapping (the job wiring, the reader, the store run) is left to the seat that owns the store. The reader leg's exclusion is not a choice: premise P6 shows hauska-engine's own test file refuses a slate this repo invents.

premisesCheckedBeforeUse.premise: A-214: a join miss is not a verified absence, so a parcel with no atom must refuse rather than read as absent.
premisesCheckedBeforeUse.status: CONFIRMED, and structurally so -- the live reader already refuses
premisesCheckedBeforeUse.evidence: The served path returns code `atom-miss` on zero atoms, so writing `absent-verified` into the cell would make the ledger claim MORE than the reader it replaces -- a cell that is wrong in the direction the program hunts (an unfounded absence). The decision core mirrors the reader's own refusal codes (`atom-miss`, `bind-conflict`, `malformed-atom`) rather than inventing new ones.

premisesCheckedBeforeUse.premise: etjStatus has four states (present / absent / unresolved / conflicting) and P-332 already serves them at the panel.
premisesCheckedBeforeUse.evidence: hauska-map@163fde3 apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/pe-etj-determination.ts resolves present/absent/unresolved and derives conflicting from raw present + cityLimits incorporated, naming both sides. The decision core reproduces that derivation rather than re-deciding it, so the ledger cell and the panel cannot disagree about which state a parcel is in.

premisesCheckedBeforeUse.premise: The cell kind a rail's cells carry is what decides whether the rail grades: value, absent-verified and refused are earned; unaccounted is not.
premisesCheckedBeforeUse.evidence: EARNED_CELL_KINDS = [value, absent-verified, refused]; the per-rail verdict returns ok only when no cell is unaccounted and at least one is earned. Consequence used deliberately: a parcel that REFUSES still lets the rail grade, which is what makes 'a join miss is refused, not absent' compatible with P-336 cutting these rails over at all (otherwise McLennan could never leave mid-cutover). Documented in the module header so a later reader does not 'fix' the refused branch into an absent one.

premisesCheckedBeforeUse.premise: The engine retrieval-api cell reader can serve the three rails once their cells are written.
premisesCheckedBeforeUse.status: BLOCKED at source -- the reader cannot be changed from hauska-engine alone
premisesCheckedBeforeUse.evidence: hauska-engine@c41a148 services/retrieval-api/src/parcel-record-slate.json is a vendored, byte-pinned copy of LDT's PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE literal (158 entries, sourceCommit 8e7218f7c81cc8a8225386558ef22ec38383650a). Its guard test (__tests__/parcel-record-slate.test.ts) pins EXPECTED_SLATE_HASH over the engine's set AND LDT_SLATE_LITERAL_SHA256 over the vendored literal, then compares the two sets IN BOTH DIRECTIONS; 'an invented pair fails' is a named assertion. Measured: 0 of the 18 (county, rail) pairs this lane cuts over are in the slate today. So adding them here fails the engine's own test until LDT's literal moves. The same test file records the precedent for how a pair is added: each pair's parcel_gate_verdict must read `pass` in the production factory store BEFORE the copy is written (that is how the 2026-09-17 six-Hays-rail resync was done). Sequence forced by that: writer applies -> verdicts flip to pass -> LDT literal gains 18 pairs -> doc_repo scripts/p299_slate_revendor.mjs re-vendors (4 places, one fact) -> engine reader serves them. Raised for the seat rather than worked around.

This is DEV_PROCESS 2.4's divergence case. The dispatch names only the doc_repo site, so it is raised, not changed here.

leaveBehindAtCp1: THE READER LEG IS CROSS-REPO AND ORDERED, not an engine change. The engine's slate is a byte-pinned vendored copy of LDT's PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE literal with a BOTH-DIRECTIONS divergence guard that fails on an invented pair. The cutover's customer-visible completion therefore needs, in order: (1) the writer applied and the three rails' parcel_gate_verdict reading `pass` in the production factory store; (2) 18 pairs added to legacy-design-tools' own literal (artifacts/api-server/src/lib/parcelRecordAllowlist.ts); (3) doc_repo scripts/p299_slate_revendor.mjs re-vendoring four places as one fact (the JSON, EXPECTED_SLATE_HASH, the LDT literal fixture, its digest); (4) the engine reader then serves them. Until (2)-(3), the cells exist and grade while the customer keeps reading the pre-cutover path -- A-193's stated behaviour for an unslated pair, and the reason a 'cells written' milestone is not a cutover.

THE SECOND POLICY SITE. hauska-factory src/lib/gate-exclusion-classifier.mjs MID_CUTOVER_RAIL_KEYS names all three rails, hand-typed, and classifies a store excluded verdict as EXCLUDED_MID_CUTOVER (a silent exclusion removed from the gate denominator). The dispatch names only the doc_repo RAIL_POLICY. Whoever lands the RAIL_POLICY diff should decide the factory list in the same change, or the two implementations will describe the same rail differently (DEV_PROCESS 2.4).

A JOIN MISS STILL LETS A RAIL GRADE, and that is load-bearing rather than incidental: refused is an earned cell, so McLennan's 0 boundary atoms grade the rail instead of pinning it open forever. Anyone who 'tidies' the refused branch into absent-verified both invents a county-wide false absence and breaks the cutover; the module header and test F1 are there to make that expensive.
